source.title: Dynamics of Awake Hippocampal-Prefrontal Replay for Spatial Learning and Memory-Guided Decision Making.

confidence_rationale: Supports MECH-319's functional intuition that replay can EXERCISE candidate trajectories (an internal cognitive search of past and future possibilities) as a process distinct from committing to behaviour -- the conceptual basis for 'exercise rule-arbitration without overwriting active weights from non-realized data'. Shows forward replay supports prospective planning and reverse replay retrospective evaluation, with a learning shift between them. Strong methods; confidence held lower because the paper shows replay DOES drive learning gradients (it writes), so it supports the exercise-without-commitment framing only by analogy, not by demonstrating a write-block.
failure_signatures: Replay here exhibits LEARNING gradients (it shapes prediction of past and future paths over training) -- it is write-active, not write-gated; this supports the 'simulate to plan' role but is evidence AGAINST a literal suppression of all updates during internal-search replay.

The 'internal cognitive search of possibilities' is a forward/reverse real-trajectory phenomenon; MECH-319's ghost/DMN non-realized passes are not directly recorded, so the exercise-without-commitment mapping is analogical.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During pauses between behavioural trajectories, reverse and forward hippocampal-prefrontal replay support an internal cognitive search of past and future possibilities, with reverse replay biased to retrospective evaluation and forward replay to prospective planning; the system shifts from reverse-replay-based retrospective evaluation to forward-replay-based prospective planning over learning, with prefrontal readout guiding decisions.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-319's purpose is to let rule-arbitration be EXERCISED during simulation/ghost/replay passes without overwriting the active rule weights from non-realized data. Shin et al. show the brain runs internally-generated replay as a search over past/future possibilities that informs decisions -- the biological instance of 'run the arbitration machinery on imagined/replayed content'. This grounds the existence of a simulate-and-evaluate mode at the hippocampal-prefrontal interface that REE places at its arbitration layer.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Crucially, this replay is shown to drive learning gradients (it writes), so it evidences the exercise/search FUNCTION of simulation but not the write-SUPPRESSION half of MECH-319; the gate that blocks updates from non-realized data remains unverified. The non-realized ghost/DMN pass MECH-319 targets is not the real-trajectory replay measured here.
mapping.source_context: Rats; simultaneous hippocampal-prefrontal ensemble recording across learning of a spatial alternation task, tracking forward/reverse replay during inter-trial pauses.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, Jadhav lab, high-quality dual-region electrophysiology across learning. Mapping fidelity moderate-low: supports the simulate-and-evaluate function but is in tension with the write-suppression claim and the ghost/DMN pass is not recorded. Hence the lowest confidence in this cluster.
